title: SDKenv compact 30-day miniplan and playbook (working notes)
content:
Purpose
---
Quick, pragmatic 30-day plan to ship a compact sdkenv (local-first dev environment + 1-click quickstart) targeted at small internal demos and early adopter teams. Focus: lowest friction to call Redwood API locally, collect minimal telemetry for onboarding KPIs, and surface common failure modes so we can iterate rapidly.

Why this exists (problem statement)
- Current onboarding takes too long: >30 minutes for many new devs.
- Multiple edge-case failures (auth, env vars, network proxy) cause drop-off during first integration.
- We need something opinionated and tiny so teams can run a sample app -> instrument -> ship a demo in a day.

Success criteria (30 days)
- 75% of internal pilot devs complete quickstart in <= 10 minutes (measured by telemetry).
- A canonical sample app (node + python) with tests and smoke harness in repo.
- Minimal telemetry dashboard with three KPIs: quickstart-completion-rate, avg-time-to-first-call, top-3 failure reasons.
- Playbook + checklist published in Drive and linked from README for external teams.

High-level scope (MVP)
- CLI installer: single script to set up environment (node, python optional), install sample app, set env vars via interactive prompt.
- Sample app: tiny chat + embedding example that demonstrates streaming and embeddings.
- Smoke tests: automated script that validates basic calls and retries (CI job).
- Telemetry: lightweight event pings (non-PII) to track progress and failure categories.
- Docs: short quickstart README + troubleshooting checklist + video clip (screen capture) for first 2 minutes.

30-day breakdown (week-by-week)
Week 0 (planning, day 0-2):
- Finalize MVP scope with PM (Arielle). Lock UX flow: CLI -> sample app -> telemetry opt-in.
- Create tickets: CLI, sample apps (node/python), smoke tests, telemetry pipeline, doc stub.
- Quick spike: prototype interactive env var setter (10–15m).

Week 1 (implementation sprint):
- CLI installer v0 (bash + cross-platform detection for mac/linux).
- Node sample app skeleton with README and local run command.
- Basic smoke test that runs locally and in CI.
- Start telemetry events: quickstart.started, quickstart.completed, quickstart.error.

Week 2 (polish + Python sample + CI):
- Add Python sample app (Flask lightweight demo).
- Integrate streaming example into node sample (show incremental output).
- CI job for smoke tests: run on PRs to sdk-samples.
- Start collecting telemetry to a staging dashboard (Grafana/Datadog).

Week 3 (docs + UX feedback loop):
- Create short 2-minute screencast and embed in README.
- Publish troubleshooting checklist with common errors and quick fixes.
- Run internal pilot with 6 engineers + get feedback.
- Iterate on CLI prompts to reduce friction; add --no-telemetry flag.

Week 4 (stability + rollout):
- Address top 3 failure reasons seen in telemetry.
- Add small vanity metrics to Console: quickstart completions per team.
- Merge PRs, update top-level docs, and announce in #dev-onboard.

Key deliverables
- sdkenv-cli (installer script + minimal docs)
- sdk-samples/quickstart-node and quickstart-python (small repos or subfolders)
- smoke-tests/quickstart-smoke.sh and CI workflow
- telemetry: schema + pipeline downstream to devops metrics dashboard
- playbook doc (this doc -> cleaned) + 2-min screencast

Telemetry & privacy
- Events (string enums): quickstart.started, quickstart.env-validated, quickstart.first-call, quickstart.completed, quickstart.error
- Payload MUST NOT include prompt content or user-provided data. Only status codes, timings, OS, CI-vs-local, and failure category.
- Opt-in default: prompt user with clear notice at install time. Provide --no-telemetry to opt-out.

Quickstart flow (user)
1) curl -sSf https://get.redwood.dev/sdkenv | bash  # interactive prompt, creates .redwood/local-config
2) cd sdks/quickstart-node
3) npm install && npm run demo
4) follow prompts to set API key (paste or open browser oauth)
5) see streaming chat demo and embedding index output

Local smoke test (dev loop)
- ./smoke-tests/quickstart-smoke.sh --env local  # runs quickstart CLI, validates first-call returns 200-like success, validates streaming tokens appear
- CI: runs same script in ephemeral runner with REDWOOD_TEST_KEY

Troubleshooting checklist (short)
- Common: API key not set -> CLI suggests `rw config set key`
- Proxy: corporate proxies may block streaming -> fallback to polling example (set RW_STREAMING=0)
- Firewall: embedding upload large file timeouts -> recommend smaller batch sizes and retry logic
- Node version mismatch -> CLI warns if node < 16 and offers nvm install snippet

Open questions / decisions to make
- Telemetry storage: use existing devops datadog funnel or funnel into Console? Short term -> Datadog staging. Long term -> Console telemetry ingest. (owner: Samir)
- Windows support: target after MVP. How many internal users need Windows? Gather list in pilot.
- OAuth vs API key UX: which to default to for demos? API key quicker but less secure.

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: telemetry accidentally logs PII -> mitigation: schema review, test cases that assert no prompt/chat text in events.
- Risk: installer script breaks corporate security scans -> mitigation: provide repo for audits + signed release.
- Risk: streaming fails on proxies -> mitigation: include fallback mode and explicit troubleshooting copy in README.

Notes to reviewers (quick)
- Please skim the smoke test script in PR #88 (linked above) and flag any missing failure cases.
- Looking for feedback on the telemetry schema (Samir), and on whether the node sample should default to streaming or polling.

Tiny implementation pointers (copyable)
- Event ping example (bash):
  curl -X POST https://telemetry-staging.redwood.dev/event -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name":"quickstart.started","version":"0.1","platform":"mac","ts":1699770000}'
- Minimal streaming fallback snippet (node):
  if (process.env.RW_STREAMING === '0') { // use polling path } else { // use streaming client }

Immediate next actions (today)
- Create tickets: CLI + node sample + smoke tests + telemetry pipeline (assigned).
- Spin up empty staging dashboard and wire a test event from my laptop.
- Get PM sign-off on scope (Arielle).

Quick links / references
- README template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-samples/blob/main/README-template.md
- Linear ticket: DEVEXP-412
- Smoke-test PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-samples/pull/88

End notes
- This is intentionally compact — we want something opinionated and tiny that we can iterate on quickly. Expect this doc to be messy; I'll trim and move a cleaned version to Confluence once pilot feedback looks good.
- If you're volunteering to pilot, ping me (Riley) in #dev-onboard and I'll add you to the testing group.

-- Riley
